posts.title: Why Is My Business Not Showing on Google Maps? 11 Fixes (2026)
posts.excerpt: Can't find your shop on Google Maps, even when you search its name? Here are the 11 reasons it happens, in the order to check them, with the fix for each.
posts.seo_title: Business Not Showing on Google Maps? 11 Fixes | U Scale
posts.seo_description: Why your business isn't showing on Google Maps or Search, and how to fix it: verification, suspension, name rules, map pin, category, reviews and more.
posts.focus_keyword: business not showing on google maps

faq.q: Why is my business not showing on Google Maps?
faq.a: The most common reasons are an unverified Business Profile, a suspended profile, a business name or address that breaks Google's guidelines, a wrong map pin, or simply a new profile that Google hasn't ranked yet. Start by checking verification and any notices in the Google Account that manages your profile.

faq.q: How long does it take for a new business to show on Google Maps?
faq.a: Google says edits can take up to 3 days to appear, and a new business can take up to a month to show in search rankings. If it's been longer, check that the profile is verified and not suspended.

faq.q: Why does my business show for its name but not for searches like near me?
faq.a: That's a ranking problem, not a visibility problem. Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence. Choose the most specific primary category, complete every part of your profile, add recent photos and earn more reviews to improve relevance and prominence.

faq.q: Can I pay Google to rank higher on Google Maps?
faq.a: No. Google states there's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Google Ads can show your business in ad slots, but organic Maps rankings have to be earned.

faq.q: Will adding keywords to my business name help me rank on Google Maps?
faq.a: It can backfire. Google's guidelines require your real-world business name without taglines, extra keywords or locations, and breaking them can get your profile suspended. Use the name on your signboard.

content.text: A customer stands outside your shop, types what you sell into Google Maps, and three other shops come up. Not yours. It happens to good, busy businesses every day in Mumbai, and the cause is almost never "Google doesn't like you". It's usually one of a handful of fixable problems: an unverified profile, a wrong category, a name that breaks the rules, or a profile Google can't trust.
This guide walks through every reason your business isn't showing on Google Maps or Search, in the order I check them during an audit, with the fix for each. Most take less than ten minutes.
The short version:

check that your profile is verified and not suspended, search while signed in to the right account, give new edits up to 3 days and new profiles up to a month, then fix your category, name, address and pin. If you show up but rank low, work on reviews, photos and complete information.
First, are you missing or just ranking low?
These are two different problems with different fixes. Search your exact business name plus your area on Google Maps (for example, "Sharma Sarees Andheri East").
You don't appear even for your own name:
it's a visibility problem. Start with fixes 1 to 6 below.
You appear for your name, but not for "saree shop near me":
it's a ranking problem. Jump to fixes 7 to 11.

attrs.alt: Flowchart: why your business is not showing on Google Maps, from verification and suspension checks to category, name, pin and ranking fixes
attrs.title: Work top to bottom. Most businesses find their problem in the first four checks.

content.text: Visibility problems: you don't show up at all
1. Your profile isn't verified
This is the big one. Google says plainly that
only verified businesses can show their business info on Maps and Search
. Open
business.google.com
while signed in. If you see a "Get verified" prompt, finish it. Google may ask for a short video of your shop, signage and tools of the trade, so film in daylight with your board clearly visible.
2. Your profile is suspended or disabled

If a profile breaks Google's guidelines, Google can disable or suspend it, and it stops showing to customers until the issue is fixed. Google sends a notice to the Google Account that manages the profile, so check that inbox (and its spam folder). Fix the cause first, usually the name, address or category, then request a review from inside your profile.
3. You're searching from the wrong account (or it's just new)

To see and manage your own profile, you need to be signed in to the Google Account linked to it. Search "my business" on Google, or open the Maps app and tap Business. Also give Google time: edits can take up to 3 days to appear, and Google says a new business can take up to a month to show in search rankings.
4. Your business name breaks the rules
Names like "Sharma Sarees – Best Saree Shop in Andheri" feel clever, but Google's
guidelines

say your name must match your real-world name, with no taglines, extra keywords or location details unless they're part of your actual name. Breaking this can get the profile suspended. Use the exact name on your signboard.
5. Your address or map pin is wrong

A typo in the address, the wrong building, or a pin dropped across the road makes Google less sure where you are. In my audits this is one of the most common problems: a misspelled street, a missing shop number, or a pin on the wrong side of a flyover. Check the full address word by word, then zoom in on the map and drag the pin onto your exact entrance.
6. There are duplicate listings of your business

Old listings created by staff, previous owners or customers split your reviews and confuse Google. Search your name and phone number on Maps. If you find a duplicate, use "Suggest an edit", then "Close or remove", then "Duplicate", or claim it and ask Google to merge it.
Ranking problems: you show up, but not where customers look
Google ranks local results on three things:
relevance
(how well your profile matches the search),
distance
(how far you are from the person searching) and
prominence
(how well known you are, including reviews and links). That's from
Google's own explanation
, which adds that there's no way to pay for a better local ranking. You can't change distance, so work on the other two.

attrs.alt: Google local ranking factors: relevance, distance and prominence, with what a business can improve for each
attrs.title: You can't move your shop closer to every customer, but you can control relevance and prominence.

content.text: 7. Your primary category is too broad or wrong

Your primary category decides which searches you're eligible for. A saree shop listed only as "Clothing store" competes with every clothes shop in the area. Pick the most specific category that describes your main business, then add up to a few secondary ones for the rest.
8. Your profile is incomplete

Fill in everything Google offers: hours, phone, website, services or products with prices, attributes like wheelchair access or online payments, and a description in plain language. Google lists complete, accurate information as the first way to improve your local ranking.
9. You have few reviews, or a low rating

Google says more reviews and positive ratings can help your local ranking, and replying to reviews shows you value feedback. If your competitors have 300 reviews and you have 12, that gap is hurting you. My guide on
how to get more Google reviews
has a 30-day plan with ready WhatsApp messages.
10. Your photos are old, few or missing

Profiles with real, recent photos look open and trustworthy. Add your shop front (so people recognise it from the street), the inside, your products, and your team. Google recommends adding photos and videos to show customers what you offer.
11. Your website doesn't back up your profile

Prominence also comes from what the rest of the web says about you. A simple website with your exact name, address and phone number, a page for each main service, and links from local directories helps Google trust your profile. If you don't have one, a
small business website
is one of the best long-term investments for local search.
Address problems that are common in Indian cities
Indian addresses are messy, and Google's systems have to match yours against what customers, delivery apps and other maps say. These are the patterns I see most often in Mumbai audits:
Missing shop or unit number.
In a building or market with 40 shops, "Sunrise Shopping Centre, Andheri East" isn't enough. Add your shop number and floor.
Different spellings of the same place.
"Gundavali", "Gundawali" and "Gundvali" may all appear online. Use the spelling on your signboard and official documents, and use it the same way everywhere.
A name in two languages.

If your board shows the name in Marathi or Hindi as well as English, use the English name in your profile and keep it identical across Google, your website and directories, rather than creating a second listing in the other language.
Landmarks inside the address.
"Opp. station" and "Near Vishal Hall" help people, but they belong in your description or directions, not in the business name.
Home-based and service businesses.

If customers don't visit you, such as a home tutor, an electrician or a caterer, set a service area and hide your home address, rather than using a fake shop address. Google's guidelines don't allow virtual offices or addresses you don't actually operate from.
What not to do when your profile is suspended
Don't create a new profile.
It's tempting, but duplicate profiles for the same business break Google's guidelines and usually make things worse.
Don't keep editing randomly.
Every edit can trigger another review. Fix the specific problem (usually the name, address or category) once, then request reinstatement.
Don't pay anyone who promises "instant reinstatement".
Only Google can reinstate a profile. Keep proof ready instead: shop photos with your signboard, a utility bill or GST certificate in the business name, and a short video of the premises.
How long until you show up on Google Maps?
Situation
What Google says
You edited your profile
Changes can take up to 3 days to show
Brand-new business profile
Can take up to a month to appear in search rankings
Suspended profile
Hidden until the issue is fixed and the profile is reinstated
Ranking improvements (reviews, photos, website)
No fixed timeline; expect weeks to months of steady work

posts.title: How to Get Your Business Recommended by ChatGPT and Google AI Mode (2026 Guide)
posts.excerpt: Customers now ask ChatGPT and Google AI Mode for shop recommendations. Here's how these AI answers pick businesses, and six practical steps to make yours easier to recommend.
posts.seo_title: Get Your Business Recommended by ChatGPT & AI Mode | U Scale
posts.seo_description: How ChatGPT and Google AI Mode choose which local businesses to recommend, and six practical steps for Indian businesses to show up in AI answers in 2026.
posts.focus_keyword: how to make my business show up on chatgpt

faq.q: How do I make my business show up on ChatGPT?
faq.a: ChatGPT search draws on what's published on the web. Make sure your website doesn't block OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot crawler, that it clearly states what you do, where and for whom, and that your name, address and phone match across Google, directories and social media. Good reviews and a complete Google Business Profile help too.

faq.q: Do I need special optimisation to appear in Google AI Overviews or AI Mode?
faq.a: Google says there are no additional requirements or special optimisations needed. Your pages need to be indexed and eligible to show a snippet in normal Google Search, so standard SEO best practices and an up-to-date Business Profile are what matter.

faq.q: Can I pay to be recommended by ChatGPT?
faq.a: No. Neither ChatGPT nor Google sells placement in their AI answers. Be wary of anyone promising guaranteed AI rankings.

faq.q: Should I block GPTBot on my website?
faq.a: That's a separate choice. OpenAI says GPTBot relates to model training, while OAI-SearchBot is what lets your pages appear in ChatGPT search. You can block GPTBot and still allow OAI-SearchBot.

faq.q: How do I know if ChatGPT is sending me customers?
faq.a: ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to links it sends people to, so these visits show up in Google Analytics. Also ask new customers how they found you.

content.text: "Suggest a good saree shop in Andheri East that's open on Sunday." More of your customers now type questions like this into ChatGPT or Google's AI Mode instead of a search box. They get one neat answer with three or four names in it. If your business isn't one of them, you don't even get the chance to lose the sale.
In Google's 2025 study of Indian festive shoppers, people used AI chatbots 7.5 times on average during a single shopping journey, and 51% said AI helped them decide (
Think with Google, 2026
). This guide explains, in plain language, how ChatGPT and Google's AI answers pick businesses to mention, and the practical steps that make yours easier to recommend.
The short version:

AI answers are built from what the web already says about you. Make sure your Google Business Profile is complete and well reviewed, your website clearly states what you do, where and for whom, your name, address and phone match everywhere, and your site allows the crawlers that AI search tools use.
How AI search picks which businesses to mention
AI assistants don't keep a secret list of favourite shops. When someone asks a question, they search the web, read what they find, and summarise it.
Google AI Overviews and AI Mode
may use what Google calls "query fan-out": they run several related searches across subtopics and sources, then build an answer with links. Google says there are
no extra requirements or special optimisations
needed to appear. Your page just has to be indexed and eligible to show a snippet in normal Google Search, and Google specifically mentions keeping your Business Profile information up to date.
ChatGPT search
can show any public website. OpenAI says that to appear in its search summaries and snippets, your site should
not block OAI-SearchBot
, its search crawler.
So the businesses AI recommends are the ones with the clearest, most consistent and most trusted information online. That's good news, because it's work you control.

attrs.alt: Diagram: how ChatGPT and Google AI Mode build an answer about local businesses from Google Business Profile, your website, reviews and directories
attrs.title: AI answers are built from your existing online presence. Fix the sources and the answers improve.

content.text: Step 1: Make your Google Business Profile complete

For Google's AI features, your Business Profile is the single most important source about your shop. Fill in your exact name, category, hours (including holiday hours), phone, website, products or services with prices, and attributes. Add fresh photos. AI answers love specifics such as "open till 10 pm", "home delivery in Andheri" and "bridal lehengas from ₹15,000", because they match the specific questions people ask.
Step 2: Earn reviews that describe what you're good at

When someone asks for "a salon that's good with curly hair", reviews that mention curly hair are exactly the evidence an AI summary looks for. You can't tell customers what to write, and you shouldn't, but asking every customer for an honest review naturally produces this kind of detail. My guide on
how to get more Google reviews
shows how, within Google's rules.
Step 3: Make your website say clearly what, where and for whom
Many small business websites are a logo, a slider and a phone number. That gives an AI almost nothing to quote. Your website should state, in plain text:
What you sell or do, in the words customers use ("plywood and laminates", not "premium surface solutions").
Where you are and which areas you serve.
Who it's for, your prices or price ranges, timings, and how to order or book.
Answers to the questions customers actually ask, written as a short FAQ.

Google advises keeping important content in text form, making pages findable through internal links, and making sure any structured data matches what's visible on the page. You don't need special AI files or markup.
Before and after: copy an AI can actually quote
Before (vague)
After (quotable)
Welcome to Sharma Sarees, your one-stop destination for quality and elegance.
Sharma Sarees is a saree shop in Andheri East, Mumbai, selling Banarasi silk, Paithani and bridal sarees from ₹2,500 to ₹60,000. Open 10 am to 10 pm, all 7 days.
We offer the best services at the best prices.
We do blouse stitching in 3 days, saree fall and pico in 1 day, and free home delivery within 5 km.
Contact us for more details.
Call or WhatsApp 98XXXXXXXX. Shop 12, Sunrise Shopping Centre, near Andheri station (East).
The "after" column answers real questions: what, where, how much, when and how. That's exactly the material AI answers are built from, and it helps human visitors decide faster too.
Step 4: Keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere

AI tools cross-check sources. If Google says "Shree Ganesh Plywood", JustDial says "Shri Ganesh Plywoods" and your Instagram bio has an old number, the AI is less confident and more likely to recommend someone else. List every place your business appears, including Google, your website, Instagram, Facebook, JustDial, IndiaMART and Swiggy or Zomato if relevant, and make them match exactly.
Step 5: Check that your website lets AI search tools in
Some website builders and security plugins block bots by default. Open
yourwebsite.com/robots.txt
in a browser, or ask your developer, and check that it doesn't block Googlebot (needed for Google's AI features) or
OAI-SearchBot
(needed for ChatGPT search). OpenAI's separate GPTBot crawler is about model training, not search, so you can make that choice separately.
ChatGPT adds
utm_source=chatgpt.com
to links it sends people to, so you can see ChatGPT visitors in Google Analytics. Google counts AI Overview and AI Mode visits in Search Console's normal Web performance report.
Step 6: Test what AI says about you, every month

Ask ChatGPT and Google AI Mode the questions your customers would ask, such as "best saree shop in Andheri East" or "plywood dealer near Gundavali metro", and note who gets mentioned. If you're missing, look at the businesses that appear: their Google profile, reviews and website are your to-do list. If an answer gets something wrong about you, the fix is almost always at the source. Correct your Google profile, website or directory listing, and AI answers follow.
Questions to test every month
Type of question
Example to ask
Category + area
Best saree shop in Andheri East
Need + area + time
Saree shop open late on Sunday near Andheri station
Budget
Bridal saree under ₹20,000 in Andheri
Comparison
Sharma Sarees vs other saree shops in Andheri: which is better?
Facts about you
What are Sharma Sarees' timings and do they deliver?
Ask in both ChatGPT and Google AI Mode, and save the answers. Over a few months you'll see whether fixes to your profile, reviews and website change what they say.
What doesn't work
Fake reviews or review swaps.
They break Google's policies and can get your profile penalised, which removes you from AI answers too.
Keyword-stuffed pages and names.
"Best cheap saree shop Mumbai Andheri" in your business name can get your Google profile suspended.
Paying someone who promises "guaranteed ChatGPT ranking".
No one controls what ChatGPT or Google says. Anyone selling a guarantee is selling a story.

Fill in your exact name, category, hours (including holiday hours), phone, website, products or services with prices, and attributes. Add fresh photos. AI answers love specifics such as "open till 10 pm", "home delivery in Andheri" and "bridal lehengas from ₹15,000", because they match the specific questions people ask.

Step 2: Earn reviews that describe what you're good at

When someone asks for "a salon that's good with curly hair", reviews that mention curly hair are exactly the evidence an AI summary looks for. You can't tell customers what to write, and you shouldn't, but asking every customer for an honest review naturally produces this kind of detail. My guide on how to get more Google reviews shows how, within Google's rules.

Step 3: Make your website say clearly what, where and for whom

Many small business websites are a logo, a slider and a phone number. That gives an AI almost nothing to quote. Your website should state, in plain text:

  • What you sell or do, in the words customers use ("plywood and laminates", not "premium surface solutions").

  • Where you are and which areas you serve.

  • Who it's for, your prices or price ranges, timings, and how to order or book.

  • Answers to the questions customers actually ask, written as a short FAQ.

Google advises keeping important content in text form, making pages findable through internal links, and making sure any structured data matches what's visible on the page. You don't need special AI files or markup.

Before and after: copy an AI can actually quote

Before (vague)

After (quotable)

Welcome to Sharma Sarees, your one-stop destination for quality and elegance.

Sharma Sarees is a saree shop in Andheri East, Mumbai, selling Banarasi silk, Paithani and bridal sarees from ₹2,500 to ₹60,000. Open 10 am to 10 pm, all 7 days.

We offer the best services at the best prices.

We do blouse stitching in 3 days, saree fall and pico in 1 day, and free home delivery within 5 km.

Contact us for more details.

Call or WhatsApp 98XXXXXXXX. Shop 12, Sunrise Shopping Centre, near Andheri station (East).

The "after" column answers real questions: what, where, how much, when and how. That's exactly the material AI answers are built from, and it helps human visitors decide faster too.

Step 4: Keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere

AI tools cross-check sources. If Google says "Shree Ganesh Plywood", JustDial says "Shri Ganesh Plywoods" and your Instagram bio has an old number, the AI is less confident and more likely to recommend someone else. List every place your business appears, including Google, your website, Instagram, Facebook, JustDial, IndiaMART and Swiggy or Zomato if relevant, and make them match exactly.

Step 5: Check that your website lets AI search tools in

Some website builders and security plugins block bots by default. Open yourwebsite.com/robots.txt in a browser, or ask your developer, and check that it doesn't block Googlebot (needed for Google's AI features) or OAI-SearchBot (needed for ChatGPT search). OpenAI's separate GPTBot crawler is about model training, not search, so you can make that choice separately.

ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to links it sends people to, so you can see ChatGPT visitors in Google Analytics. Google counts AI Overview and AI Mode visits in Search Console's normal Web performance report.

Step 6: Test what AI says about you, every month

Ask ChatGPT and Google AI Mode the questions your customers would ask, such as "best saree shop in Andheri East" or "plywood dealer near Gundavali metro", and note who gets mentioned. If you're missing, look at the businesses that appear: their Google profile, reviews and website are your to-do list. If an answer gets something wrong about you, the fix is almost always at the source. Correct your Google profile, website or directory listing, and AI answers follow.

Ask in both ChatGPT and Google AI Mode, and save the answers. Over a few months you'll see whether fixes to your profile, reviews and website change what they say.

What doesn't work

  • Fake reviews or review swaps. They break Google's policies and can get your profile penalised, which removes you from AI answers too.

  • Keyword-stuffed pages and names. "Best cheap saree shop Mumbai Andheri" in your business name can get your Google profile suspended.

  • Paying someone who promises "guaranteed ChatGPT ranking". No one controls what ChatGPT or Google says. Anyone selling a guarantee is selling a story.

faq.q: Do Instagram posts show up on Google?
faq.a: Yes. Since 10 July 2025, public photos, videos and reels from professional (business or creator) Instagram accounts of people over 18 can be indexed by search engines such as Google and Bing. Posts from 1 January 2020 onwards are included.

faq.q: How do I stop my Instagram posts showing on Google?
faq.a: Turn off the search engine option in your Instagram privacy settings, make your account private, or switch from a professional account to a personal one. Content that's already indexed can take time to disappear from search engines.

faq.q: Do hashtags help Instagram posts rank on Google?
faq.a: Not much on their own. Search engines rely on the words in your caption, alt text and profile. A clear caption that says what the product is, where you are and the price does far more than a long list of hashtags.

faq.q: Should a local shop focus on Instagram or Google Business Profile?
faq.a: Both, and connect them. Many shoppers see a brand on Instagram and then check it on Google before visiting, so your Instagram and Google profiles should show the same name, prices, photos and timings.
